output.prose:
Procedures performed: Agreed invoice totals to the general ledger, compared invoiced quantities and dates with bills of lading, and traced invoice totals to subsequent bank deposits where available. Reviewed shipment timing for year-end cutoff and compared invoice details for potential duplication.

Samples tested: [[item:INV-1028]], [[item:INV-1029]], [[item:INV-1030]], [[item:INV-1034]], [[item:INV-1047]], [[item:INV-1068]], [[item:INV-1088]], [[item:INV-1110]], [[item:INV-1111]], [[item:INV-1112]], [[item:INV-1113]], [[item:INV-1114]], [[item:INV-1115]], [[item:INV-1116]], and [[item:INV-1117]].

Results: All invoice totals agreed to the general ledger. Where shipping and bank evidence was available, shipped quantities and deposit amounts agreed to the invoices. No customer letter or warehouse note was provided to substantiate a bill-and-hold arrangement.

Exceptions: [[item:INV-1030]] matched [[item:INV-1029]] on customer, invoice date, product, quantity, and total. Only the latter had a supporting bill of lading and bank deposit. The amount at risk of duplicate recognition is [[ev:ev-INV-1030-invoice_amount]]. For [[item:INV-1113]], the invoice date was [[ev:ev-INV-1113-invoice_date]], but the full quantity shipped after year-end on [[ev:ev-INV-1113-ship_date]]. The subsequent deposit matched the invoice total of [[ev:ev-INV-1113-invoice_amount]] but did not support recognition before year-end.

Conclusion: No other exceptions were identified in the sample. Confirm whether the potential duplicate represents a separate sale and assess the adjustments needed for the duplicate and cutoff exceptions before closing the test.
